k8d80k-flight-status-card-microinteracti.summary: One white flight card, 962x311 px with about 60 px corner radius, sits centred on a flat cool-grey (#c7c8cf) frame. It has no visible shadow or outline. The card has three columns. Left: "JFK" in large bold dark grey (#404040), "New York" under it in mid grey (#878994), and a pale lavender pill (#f0f0f6, fully rounded) holding a grey outlined clock and "03:20 PM". The digits are monospaced with slashed zeros. Right: the same set right-aligned, "LAX", "Los Angeles" and "09:40 PM". Centre: "ON TIME" in an orange-red (#f63c00) monospaced face, then a route row with two thin grey tracks (4 px tall, round caps) either side of a solid orange plane icon flying right. Small orange speed dashes sit behind the plane. Under the row is "6h 10m" in dark grey sans. Motion: from 0 to 1 s the card holds at rest. A short orange segment slides left along the left track and wraps back in from the right, like the ground streaming past. At about 1.03 s a camera zoom starts, centred on the card at about (720, 562). It eases in and out until about 2.3 s and ends near 3.8x, with only the centre stack in view: ON TIME, the route row and 6h 10m. While the camera moves, the outer content smears with horizontal motion blur. The card's top and bottom edges leave the frame at about 2.17 s. From about 2.4 to 5.5 s the zoomed view holds, drifting slightly closer. The orange segment keeps streaming left along the left track (about 200 px/s at this zoom, one pass about every 2 s). The plane rocks: its wings foreshorten and spread as it banks, and the speed dashes flicker and shift. From about 5.6 to 6.95 s the camera eases back out with the same blur, and the card is back at rest from 7 to 8 s.

1g1yor-minimal-kanban-board-component.summary: A light, minimal Kanban board on an off-white #f9f9f9 page, 1080x1080. Top left: the title "Billing v2" (about 20px, near-black, medium weight) with a muted grey "12 cards" beside it. Top right: a pill segmented control "Status | Swimlanes" (about 143x34, light grey track). The active segment is a white pill with warm orange-brown text. Below are four equal columns, each about 253px wide with 12px gutters, starting at x 16/281/546/811 and running from y 166 to 1016. Each column is a very light grey rounded panel (radius about 16, soft edge). The headers above them read "Backlog 4", "In progress 3/3", "In review 2/2" and "Done 3", each with a grey count and a thin "+" at the right. Cards are white, 235px wide, radius about 10, with a hairline grey border and a faint shadow. Each card has a monospaced grey ID (e.g. "BIL-142"), a coloured-dot tag at top right (orange Billing, purple Design, blue API, olive Lifecycle), a 14px dark title on one or two lines, a grey meta row (calendar date, checklist fraction, "N pt") and a 22px round photo avatar at bottom right. Each column ends with a grey "+ Add card". Motion is a cursor demo in three acts. (1) 0–0.4s: the cursor hovers BIL-142 at the top of Backlog and the card's border darkens. From 0.5s it is picked up: it lifts, tilts about 3–4°, and gets a warm peach border and shadow. The remaining Backlog cards slide up 124px. While it is over In progress (about 0.9s), that column gets an orange outline and beige tint, its count turns amber "4/3" with an "Over limit" pill, and a dashed placeholder opens. It then moves to In review, where a dashed slot opens under BIL-124 (1.6s). It drops at about 1.85s and settles flat. In review now reads amber "3/2 Over limit" and its panel stays beige; Backlog reads 3. (2) 4.0–5.2s: BIL-128 is dragged the same way from the top of In progress to the top of Done. In progress closes up 107px and reads "2/3"; the Done cards shift down 106px and Done reads "4". (3) About 6.0–6.5s: the cursor moves to the toggle and clicks "Swimlanes" (about 6.5s); the white pill slides to Swimlanes. From 6.6 to 7.2s the board regroups into four assignee lanes ("Emma Collins 4", "Marcus Johnson 3", "Chloe Nguyen 2", "Daniel Kim 3"), each with an avatar header and one rounded cell per column. Cards glide into their lane cells and empty cells stay as blank grey panels. The board then holds to 8.8s.

1ipk9s-flyingpress-bento-feature-grid.summary:
A light, centred feature section on a near-white #f2f2f4 page. At top centre is a small white pill eyebrow, "Why FlyingPress" (y≈67–97). Below it is a large near-black headline, "Real-time WordPress optimization" (≈48px, tight tracking, y≈112–160), and a one-line grey subtitle (y≈184). Under these sits a 3×2 bento grid of white cards, each 360×382 with ≈20px radius and 15px gutters (columns x=45/420/795, rows y=234/631). The upper part of each card is an illustration on a soft peach-to-orange wash, some with a faint dotted texture. Each card ends with a 20px dark title and two lines of 14px grey body text at the bottom left. The whole thing runs on a 6 s loop with 2 s beats:
(1) "Easy to Use": a FlyingPress plugin card. It shows "Active" with an orange "✓ Optimized" button and three green-checked chips until ≈2.3s. It then flips to "Inactive" / "Optimize my site" with empty-circle chips. A cursor glides onto the button at ≈3.9s and clicks it at ≈4.4s; the label blurs, and by ≈5s it is back to Active.
(2) "Fewer Settings": three toggle pills (Page Caching, Image Optimization, Critical CSS). They switch off and on, collapse into a single stacked "All optimizations" pill at ≈2.5–4.3s, then fan back out with all three on.
(3) "Core Web Vitals": three metric pills (CLS, LCP, INP) with ring gauges and Good/Poor/Needs-work badges. The middle pill is enlarged. Every ≈2s (at 0.4, 2.45, 4.4, 6.4) the list scrolls up one pill, and the ring values count and recolour.
(4) "All in One": a large white arch cut into the orange wash. Faint app-icon tiles sit behind it and fade in and out, with a glossy orange FlyingPress app icon at the bottom of the funnel.
(5) "Great Support": an orange user avatar centred in concentric peach rings, with three small white icon bubbles (?, headset, cursor) orbiting it clockwise.
(6) "Compatibility": a glossy FlyingPress icon in the middle row between a cloud tile and a "+" tile. The top row of logo tiles (W, Kinsta, grid logo) slides left and the bottom row (Elementor, cloud, +) slides right as a continuous marquee.
The header and the card frames never move.

tznig8-dashboard-layout.summary: A light SaaS admin screen, "FlowAI" Team Members, shown as one app window floating on a #f3f3f3 page. At rest (4.7s) the window sits at [137,125,1166,830]. It has rounded ~16px corners, a white surface and a soft wide grey shadow. A 185px near-white sidebar on the left holds the logo, two dashed-circle section labels ("Workspaces", "Agent Managements"), 10 nav rows with thin grey line icons (the active "Team Members" row sits in a grey pill with a green "35+" badge), a "Workflow Runs" list with 4 coloured square icons, a usage card and a user row. The main area (#f4f4f4) has a 50px top bar, a page title with three buttons on the right (the last is a dark "+ Invite Member"), a white panel with segmented tabs and 4 grey stat cards, and a white table panel. The table has 3 filter dropdowns, a grey header row, 10 member rows with small round portrait avatars and pastel status pills, and pagination. A faint vertical-tick band runs under the main area. Type is a neutral grotesk, dark grey on light, with 11–13px UI text. The motion is a staged reveal driven by a dark arrow cursor. 0–0.3s: a cut from the finished dashboard to the window magnified ~1.77x, with only the logo visible. 0.35–1.65s: the window rises ~333px while sidebar rows blur-fade in one after another from the top. The cursor points at Team Members. 2.25–2.7s: the camera pulls back to 1x and the header and title blur in. 2.9–4.7s: the stat cards and then the table rows blur-fade in top to bottom, and the stat numbers count up (Seats Used reads 34/48 at 4.2s and 35/50 at 4.7s). ~5s: the cursor clicks Invite Member. 5.25–6.05s: the camera pushes in on the dashboard, which blurs and washes out, and a centred "Invite Team Members" modal (grey shell, inner white panels, ~20px radius) appears, its fields staggering in. The cursor types name@company.com, picks the Admin role (blue outline) and clicks Send Invitations. 9.85–10.55s: the modal dissolves, the dashboard un-blurs at a magnified scale, and by ~11.2s it zooms back to the rest layout, so the clip loops.

j0xwyn-wellness-app-animated-onboarding.summary: Three iPhone screens, each 300 x 650 with a ~36px corner radius, sit side by side on a near-white #fcfcfc canvas. Their tops are at y≈241, centred vertically, with ~65px gaps: a splash screen at x=166, a sign-in screen at x=530 and a dashboard at x=895. The splash shows a pale grey (#ededed) ground with a huge soft white spiral ribbon. In the middle is a black spiral 'n' logo over the black wordmark 'ChoosingHealth®'. The sign-in screen is a full-bleed photo of a woman in beige activewear sitting on a grey floor. Over it are a white three-line headline 'Today is / the day, you / chose health.', a small white line 'You're here. That's what matters.', two solid white pill buttons (Apple, Google), an 'or' divider, a dark translucent frosted pill 'Continue with Email', and grey legal text. The dashboard has a light-grey ground with a logo, a bell with a pink badge and an avatar. Below them are a white 'Your journey' card holding a soft pink blurred arc with a glowing red dot at day 7, two white pills ('Quick Win', 'Mark as Moved'), a 'Your Next Step' photo card 'Tone & Sculpt your upper' with a coral 'Start' pill, and a tab bar (Home, Library, Community). Motion: from 0 to ~1.6s the three phones fade in from heavy gaussian blur while drifting up into place. The centre phone appears first; the left one follows, slightly tilted; the right one comes last, rising ~220px from below. Screen content then fades in and sharpens between ~1.0 and 2.2s: the splash logo and wordmark, the headline, then the buttons and the dashboard cards. At ~2.0–2.3s the pink journey arc sweeps in around its dot and the workout card sharpens. From ~2.3s to ~4.9s pink, magenta and lilac confetti strips fall through the dashboard phone only. From 5.0s to the end everything holds still.

1cc6s3-switch-ui.summary: One switch, centred on a flat near-white page (#fafafa). There is no text. The track is a wide rounded rectangle [522,378,462,324] with a corner radius of about 92 px. It is a flat sage colour (#c1cdcb) when off, with a slightly darker inset edge along the bottom and right. When on, it is a green vertical gradient (#138726 at the top to #439846 at the bottom). A faint white glow strip sits just under its bottom edge. The knob is a tall rounded square that overhangs the track by 12 px on the top, bottom and outer side. From the outside in, it has three layers. First, a translucent dark ring about 11 px wide: light grey (#b5b6b6) at the top, darker (#8f8f8f) at the bottom, and it turns dark green where it lies over the green track. Second, a pure white bezel about 22 px wide. Third, an inner face with a soft gradient from #fafafa down to #f3f3f3 and a radius of about 60. A large soft grey drop shadow falls below the knob, out to about y=840. A macOS hand or arrow cursor drives the clip. The knob never slides as one rigid piece; it stretches like elastic. Hovering widens it by about 24 px toward the track's centre (off: right edge 810→834; on: left edge 696→672). Clicking ON at about 4.15 s first throws the knob's right edge out to the far end (834→996 by 4.25 s, so it covers the whole track), and the track turns green underneath. Then the left edge catches up (510→672, about 4.3–4.4 s). Clicking OFF at about 5.8 s does the same in reverse: the left edge reaches back to 510 by 5.9 s, with a thin green sliver still showing at the left, then the right edge pulls in to 834 by about 6.0–6.1 s while the track turns sage again. Pressing and holding stretches the knob part of the way: at 9.5 s the left edge is at 562 while the right edge stays at 996. From about 10.6 s to 17.3 s it toggles rapidly with the same stretch-then-follow motion, then rests off.

zcjkb5-interactive-personal-site.summary: A screen recording of a minimal personal site on an off-white page (#f9f9f9), shown through a camera that zooms in and out (the zooms, motion blur and purple wallpaper are video editing, not page content). Zoomed in (0–5.3s), the page is a left-aligned column at x≈415: a cut-out black-and-white head-and-shoulders photo of Ahmed Dahbi (≈290×395 px, bottom edge cut in a soft arc), the serif name "Ahmed Dahbi" (≈95 px cap-to-baseline, near-black #181818), then a grey monospace bio. The face is a set of photos of different head poses that swap instantly to look toward the cursor (right, up-right, left, down). At ≈5.3s the theme toggles to dark (#121212 page, light #e8e8e8 type) and the portrait becomes a full-colour photo, still tracking the cursor. At ≈7.95s it is back to light and the camera pulls out to show the whole page inside a rounded window: portrait, name, three-line bio, a small square theme toggle at top right, a five-row accordion (> ABOUT, CAREER, ADVISORY, SIDE PROJECTS, BOOKSHELF) with hairline dividers, a centred black "How I can help" button, and Twitter / LinkedIn / Email links. Clicking BOOKSHELF (≈11.7s) opens a 3D shelf: one book pulled forward showing its cover, four coloured spines standing behind it, a soft grey cast shadow on the floor to the right, ← / → square buttons, a "02 / 09" counter, title, author, an "Inspect ↗" button, and nine tick marks with the active one in red. The arrow steps through Understanding Comics → Le Monde Sans Fin → The Wizard & the Prophet; clicking the book opens a detail view split by a vertical hairline, the book on the left as a real 3D hardcover the cursor orbits (16.6→17.1s it turns from front cover to back cover, showing cream page edges and a green band), and on the right "← Back to shelf", the serif title, author, a monospace blurb, a rust underlined "View on Goodreads ↗" link and a pale hint line. Radii are small (≈4–6 px on buttons, ≈12 px on the window); all type is serif for names and titles, monospace for everything else.

1odjuy-google-calendar-empty-state.summary: A single centred empty state sits on an off-white (#fafafa) canvas with a 1px grey top edge. The background has faint horizontal dotted rules about 24px apart that fade out radially from the centre, so they only show in a soft oval around the content. The centre column holds three things. First, a cluster of three rounded-square white tiles (about 62px, radius about 14px, soft drop shadow, each tilted a little differently): a Google "G" on the left, a grey plug-and-socket glyph in the middle that sits higher, and a dark-green squiggle on the right. Below that is a semibold dark green-grey title, "Connect your Google account", then a two-line grey body paragraph, then a green pill button reading "Connect Google" with an arrow cursor resting on its right end. All of it is centred on x≈547. The motion tells one story and then loops. At about 1.5s the button label is replaced by a small white tick spinner. Between 2.65s and 2.8s the button fades out and the whole stack slides down about 49px to recentre. The middle tile's plug becomes a dashed ring, the title becomes "Syncing your calendar" and the body becomes one line, "Your meetings will appear here once it's done". From about 3s to 7.8s a dark grey pie wedge fills clockwise inside the dashed ring. At about 7.8s it turns into a solid green circle with a white check, and the two side tiles fade to about half strength. From 8.0s to 8.5s the text crossfades to "Calendar synced" / "Your meetings are ready". From about 9.3s the empty state fades away. Between 9.5s and 10.2s a full-width meeting list fades in row by row from the top: a pale-green "Coming up 4" header band, four upcoming rows, a grey "Earlier 208" band, then dated rows (date, time, small app logo, title, avatar stack on the right). The cursor becomes a hand over the highlighted "Ashford pilot checkpoint" row. At 11.9–12.05s the list crossfades straight back to the original "Connect Google" empty state.

826xtq-minimal-file-dropzone-ui.summary: A single centred dropzone card on a flat #f7f7f7 page, 1080x1080. The card spans about x 161 to 911 and y 323 to 697 (750x375). It has a radius of about 24 px, a thin light-grey dashed border, and a near-white #fdfdfd fill. A faint grey dot grid sits on a 16 px pitch, with dots of about 2 px. The content is centred in one column: a 70 px white rounded-square tile (radius about 18, 1 px light-grey border) holding a grey outlined file-with-up-arrow icon, then a bold near-black title "Drop a file here" (~22 px), then a grey subline "Documents, media and archives · 20 MB limit" (~16 px). The story is a macOS file drag. About 1.1 s in, a blue Finder-style filename chip "harsh-singh-resume.pdf" with a green + badge and an arrow cursor slides in from the bottom-left. Around 1.4 s the card enters its drag-active state: the fill greys to about #f2f2f2, the dashed border darkens to mid-grey, the dots darken, the icon turns black and the title becomes "Almost there". The card leans a few px toward the cursor, magnetically. When the cursor enters the card (about 2.5 to 3.1 s), the title crossfades with a blur to "Let go to upload". A halo about 100 px across follows the cursor, where the grid dots grow to about 4 px and turn mid-grey. The cursor leaves (3.6 to 3.95 s, back to "Almost there") and re-enters (4.45 to 4.8 s, "Let go to upload"). At about 5.45 s the file is dropped. A red halftone dot ring bursts outward from the icon tile: thick red dots on the ring front fade to grey at its edges, and a soft pink radial glow fills the inside. The ring sweeps past the card edges by about 5.9 s. The icon tile swaps to a white 80 px tile with a red "PDF" badge, and the text becomes a green check plus "Uploaded successfully", "harsh-singh-resume.pdf" and a monospace "PDF · 40 KB". About 6.2 s, two light pill buttons fade in: "Remove" (trash icon) and "Upload another" (upload icon). The final state from 6.5 to 8.5 s is a grey #f2f2f2 card with no visible dot grid and a very faint dashed border. It holds still.

uyag6q-cinema-mobile-app.summary: A single iPhone mockup (silver-rimmed, black screen, ~300x627 px, centred at x 210-510, y 45-672) on a flat #f2f2f2 canvas walks through a dark cinema ticket flow with yellow (#f4d63e) accents. Screen 1 (0-1.55s) "Who's going?": back arrow, a red Bad Guys poster thumbnail with logo, year/genre/runtime and IMDb 7.7, a hairline divider, the title and grey subtitle, three soft-shaded face characters (teal blob, yellow rounded square, salmon circle with glasses) that blink/change expression, a −/3/+ stepper with dark grey circular buttons, and a full-width yellow Continue pill; a translucent touch dot taps Continue at ~1.1s. 1.6-2.2s the page swaps to "Where to Sit?": the title settles near y 157, a curved cinema screen grows from a thin glowing arc into a 232x52 curved band playing footage with a warm light spill below, and the seat grid (8 rows: 8 seats then 7 rows of 10, grey with brighter available seats) fades in top-down; a "3 Seats Together" dropdown pill and dim helper text sit below and Continue is disabled dark grey. ~3.4s a tap on row 5 seat 5 turns three seats yellow, a dark "Row 5 · 3 Seats" badge with three mini face avatars pops above them, and Continue turns yellow (by 4.2s). The screen footage keeps playing (turning gold). ~6.7s Continue is tapped; 7.3-7.7s the page dims and a #2a2a2a Checkout sheet (radius ~24) slides up from the bottom to top y≈258 with movie row, date/seat row, Pay With card, Total $21.99 and a yellow Pay pill. ~9.2s Pay is tapped; 9.65-9.75s the sheet and page vanish for a dark skeleton ticket (notched corners and side notches) with a "Generating your ticket" pill and spinner, held until 13.75s, when the full poster ticket with a dark barcode stub appears. 15.1-15.4s the ticket flips around its vertical axis (edge-on at 15.2s), then 16.1-16.6s it settles smaller and higher with its lower poster fading to black, "The Bad Guys" title, date, Screen/Row/Seats 2/5/4 - 6 details, a white Manage RSVP pill, a dark bottom card with QR code, and a close X; this end state holds still to 18.73s.

1xfcpx-cute-button-figma-tutorial.summary: A Figma-style build-up of one soft, puffy app button on a flat pale gray-lavender canvas (#ecedf2), with a dark pill caption bottom-centre naming each step. 0.4–1.1s: a thin blue (#3aa0e0-ish) 1px outline draws itself clockwise from the top-left of a 350x352 squircle centred at x 288 (box 113,184 to 463,536, corner radius ~128 px, i.e. 'Radius 48' on 132). 1.1–1.5s it fills flat gray-blue (#d0d5e0) and the outline goes. ~1.5–2.5s an inner white light sweeps down from the top edge ('Gradient · Inner light 14 · White 80%'), giving a white-to-pale-gray vertical gradient. ~3.5–5s a soft blurred white sheen sits on the upper half ('Sheen · White 62% to 0 · Blur 4'). ~5–6s a layered soft drop shadow appears under it ('Shadow · Y 5, 14, 24 · Blur 7, 18, 32'). ~6.2–7.8s a heart outline draws in blue inside, fills white, and gets a 16px pale gray ring ('Icon · Ring 16'). 8.2–8.55s the press: the whole button tints pink (#f7a6c4 body, #e0306a heart, #f590b4 ring), squashes wide then stretches tall and settles ('Press · Colour from the icon · 180 ms'). 9.4–10.55s 'Repeat × 4': the pink button shrinks and slides to top-left while three white clones fan out into a 2x2 grid of 186 px buttons with a 38 px gap. ~10.6–11.8s outlines draw a moon (top-right), drop (bottom-left) and leaf (bottom-right), they fill white with gray rings, then each tints in turn with the same squash: purple 11.9s, blue 12.35s, green 12.8–13.1s. The caption fades by ~13.3s and the four candy-coloured buttons hold to the end. Type is a small sans (Inter-like) in white on a near-black pill with full radius.

1dftym-click-drag-interaction.summary: A minimal 404 page on flat near-white: in the upper half a vector "face" — a thick light-grey upside-down U arch (x 238–623, y 140–335, ~48px legs, flat #f0f0f0 fill and 1px #888 stroke) over two 78px circles at (379,289) and (482,289) — shown as if selected in a vector editor, with hairline bezier handles ending in hollow diamonds and hollow circle anchors (6 on the arch, 4 per circle). Below, in one centred column: "Page Not Found" (near-black, medium, ~18px, y≈452), the grey subtitle "Every component accounted for, except this page." (y≈487), and a flat #eceaeb pill "← Back to Home" (330,534,202x47) with no border or shadow. Nothing moves on its own; a macOS cursor (arrow, turning into a grab hand) drags handles and the shapes reshape live: the outer-left handle is pulled out and around (1.3–3.6s), the inner-left handle reshapes the left leg (5–7.3s), the left circle stretches into a tall 78x121 ellipse (8.0–8.9s), the right circle squashes into a flat 80x30 ellipse (9.9–10.1s), the outer-right handle is pulled up to ~(639,112) (11.6–13.8s), and the top handle is tugged at the end (14.3s on). Text and button never change.

1w3d9n-polished-text-animations.summary: A product page for a text-animation agent skill, shown as a white page card (131,90 to 1788, running off the bottom edge) floating on a soft, static blue backdrop gradient (periwinkle top, cyan glow on the left near y 600, deeper blue on the right). The card is split by 1px #eaeaeb hairlines into a fixed 480px left column and a two-column grid of 590x331 cells on the right (columns 611-1201 and 1201-1788, rows at 90/419/751). The left column, top-aligned with a 36px inset, holds a small monospace "SKILLS.md" label with a cube icon, a three-line ~52px bold near-black headline "Crafted [curve tile] text / animations for / AI workflows" with a small soft-shaded squircle tile showing a black bezier curve and a blue dot, two grey 18px paragraphs, a light grey rounded command pill "$ npx skills add pixel-point/animate-" whose end fades out, with a copy icon, and at the bottom "Made by Pixel Point." and a round moon theme button. Each grid cell holds one centred phrase (~34px semibold, dark grey, two-line phrases have a lighter second line) and every cell keeps cycling its phrase with a different text animation: per-word gaussian blur resolving left to right, words rising and fading in with a stagger, word-by-word fade, letters erasing, and fade/scale. A mouse cursor hovers cells: the hovered cell tints to #f7f7f7, shows a 16px copy icon in its top-right corner and replays its animation. From about 3.85s to 5.6s the grid scrolls up exactly three rows (~993px) under the fixed left column while a thin dark overlay scrollbar shows at x≈1783; it holds until about 9.1s and then scrolls again in two moves (9.1-9.85s, 10-10.75s). The backdrop, card edges and left column never move.

jwsub4-ascii-page-transition.summary: A split landing page (1920x1080) swaps to a blog page and back, with a full-screen ASCII glyph dissolve as the transition. Home page: the left half (0–968) is warm cream #edeae2. On it sit a small mono caps tagline at x=80, a three-line ~84px dark grotesk headline "The Sanity / setup agents / don't reinvent.", a grey 17px paragraph, a mono caps note, two dark rounded buttons "GET" and "ACCESS" at y=704, and three columns of mono stats near y=1001/1023. The right half (968–1920) is near-black #212120, filled with a typographic spiral: concentric rings of white monospace "THE CONTENT ARCHITECTURE" text around (1440,540) over faint dotted rings. Its characters scramble in place while the ring layout holds. Floating chrome: a centred dark nav pill (698,15,524x56) with a dithered border, a hatched logo square, and grey mono links FEATURES · THE REPO · SHOWCASE · PRICING · FAQ · BLOG. Also a page-thumbnail box at top right, a white "CLICK & HOLD" tag near the cursor, "LEARN MORE" and "+" controls at bottom right, and a black 5-slot pager pill on the seam at x≈957–977, y≈972–1039. Motion: the cursor clicks BLOG at about 1.2s. From 1.30s, blocky blobs of dense ASCII glyphs (cells about 12x17px, grey-to-white characters on black) grow out over the page with stair-stepped edges. They cover the whole frame by about 1.68s and hold as a flickering glyph field through about 2.0s. The field then breaks into blobs and clears (about 2.0–2.45s) to show the dark "Knowledge Hub" blog page: a centred 920px column at x=500 with a 48px white title, two grey intro paragraphs, 1px dividers at y≈409 and 660, and two article entries. BLOG is highlighted in the nav, and a faint ASCII band sits behind the footer "© 2026 THE CONTENT ARCHITECTURE". This holds until about 4.25s. The logo is clicked, and glyphs flood back over the blog page (4.3–4.8s). The cream home page then breaks through in blobs from about 5.0s and fills column x=600 from y≈550 outward by 5.55s. Once it settles, the spiral rebuilds from sparse scattered letters (5.8s) back to dense rings (about 6.55s). The footer stats type in again one at a time, with a block cursor (5.8s "NEXT 16.X" only, 6.35s "SANITY V6" and "T█", 6.9s "TS: STRICT").

e1gket-design-stack-data-table.summary: A single light-grey rounded card (#ececec, ~40px radius, 82..1633 x 159..925) is centred on a near-white #f7f7f7 page. Its top strip has a blue rounded-square app icon, the title "Design Stack" in dark medium sans (~30px), and undo/redo arrows at the right, pale grey when disabled. Inset in the card sits a white table (~36px radius, faint shadow, hairline #e5e5e5 grid). The table has a checkbox column, then Tool, Category, Website and Renews headers, each with a small grey glyph and mid-grey label. There are five 95px rows: Figma, Linear, Vercel, Framer and Loom, each with its brand logo, a tinted category pill (purple Design, blue Issue tracking, grey Hosting, pink Website, green Video), an underlined domain link and a renewal date. The footer reads "+ Add row" on the left and "Double-click a cell to edit" on the right in mid grey. The clip is a recorded cursor session in which every change is an instant state swap, not a slide. At 1.0s Linear is checked: its box turns black with a white tick, the row tints pale blue, the header box shows a black minus, and the footer becomes "1 selected · Delete (red, trash icon) · Clear". At 2.0s the rows re-sort by Tool (blue up arrow), and at 3.1s by Category (the arrow moves to Category). Then come blue cell outlines on B2 (4.1s) and B4 (4.95s), with the cell reference shown at bottom right. At 5.9s an opaque white dropdown with a soft shadow opens, listing Design / Issue tracking / Hosting / Website / Video, with the current value in blue. At 7.05s Hosting is picked: Loom's pill becomes Hosting, Loom re-sorts to row 3, and undo darkens. Next, Loom's Website cell is edited: "https://loom.com" in a double blue ring at 9.3s, cleared by 9.8s. Delete at ~11.55s removes Linear, and the card shrinks by one row (top +47, bottom −47) in ~0.2s. Add row at ~12.35s appends an empty row with a caret in its Tool cell and the card grows back. Undo at ~14.1s removes that row, shrinking the card again, and redo turns dark.

151zb7-snapping-deal-table-groups.summary: A light, quiet CRM 'Deals' table sits as a tall white card (#fafafa, 1px pale-grey border, ~16px radius) inside a larger warm-grey rounded stage (#efefef, ~32px radius, faint grain) on an off-white page (#f7f7f7). The card's right, top and bottom edges stay fixed (right ≈1285, top 64, bottom 1015); only its left edge is dragged with a ◂|▸ resize cursor, so the card stretches left and right across the 25.9s. Inside: a header row (three-circle 'Deals' icon, 'Deals' in dark medium type, muted '11' count, filter icon at the far right), then four grouped sections, each with a rounded light-grey header band (status icon + name + small grey count pill: Proposal 3 with a dashed green ring, Demo 3 with a dotted green ring, Leads 3 with a hollow pale-green ring, Closed Won 2 with a filled green check) followed by its deal rows on a 47px pitch: 16px company logo tile, name in dark type, amount, right-hand date and a 14px round owner photo. The table snaps between three layouts by width: compact (under ~620px wide) shows 'Name $450 … 27 Aug ●'; medium (~700–780px) moves the amount into its own column as 'USD 450', moves the date into a centre column and puts tag / calendar / smiley column icons into the group header bands; wide (~785px and up) adds a fourth people column (@ icon) holding overlapping contributor avatar stacks. When the width crosses a threshold the cells slide to their new columns with a top-to-bottom stagger, row by row, the '$450' and 'USD 450' labels cross-fading as they travel, so mid-transition the upper rows are already settled while the lower rows still show overlapping ghosted text. The drag goes: hold compact (0–1.45s), widen to medium (~1.5–2.45s) and wide (~2.55–3.25s), back to medium and compact (~3.5–4.5s), then back and forth through ~6–9.3s, with holds at compact (~9.3–10.5s), medium (~13.85–15.5s) and compact (~18.8–21.95s), and finally the cursor moves into the card and hovers a row (~24.5s), which shows a grey hover band.

1pekjm-playful-character-picker-sheet.summary: A single illustrated object centred on a flat near-white (#f6f6f9) canvas with a small grey home-indicator pill at bottom centre (954-1006, 1060-1070): a paper-towel/receipt roll drawn in thick royal-blue (#2826c8) outline, with a 3D box bracket on its left (672-748, 412-556) and a small tab on its right (1272-1288, 450-526). The roll's top is a cylinder (thick curved side strokes down to ~y 640) and below it straight paper hangs to a zig-zag torn bottom edge. On the paper sit list rows separated by lavender dashed lines: a 126 px rounded-square avatar with a 5 px blue border and flat-colour character illustration, a bold blue sans name (Daniel, Alex...), and on the chosen row a blue outlined check circle at the right. Collapsed state (rest 0.9-3.45 s): roll 758-1262 x 316-790, two rows, Daniel then Alex with a check. Motion: 0.15-0.85 s the paper prints down from the roll, overshooting its bottom edge to ~860 at 0.5 s and settling back to ~785, while rows ride down with it. A cursor comes in from bottom-left and clicks Alex. 3.5-4.45 s the whole roll shrinks to a narrow tall receipt (832-1160 x, top 118) that unrolls off the bottom of the frame, now listing Mia, Marcus, Leo, Emma, Daniel, Alex at a ~152 px row pitch with 80 px avatars. The hovered row (Emma) gets a pale lavender (#e8e9f8) band. 5.35-7.0 s the list scrolls inside the paper to show Ethan, Oliver, James at the top, then scrolls back so Lucas and Noah show below Alex. At ~8.05 s clicking Emma moves the check to Emma and tears the receipt along a zig-zag line just under Emma's row. 8.1-9.55 s the lower piece (Daniel, Alex, Lucas, Noah) drops out of the bottom of the frame while the upper part retracts back into the wide collapsed roll, which then rests (9.7-10.65 s) showing Leo then Emma with the check. 10.7-11.65 s it expands again into the narrow receipt, which now ends at Emma (check) with a torn edge, listing Oliver, James, Mia, Marcus, Leo, Emma.

50lhy3-liquid-glass-lens-demo.summary: A single-column demo page for liquid-glass components on a warm off-white ground (#f2f0eb), set in a monospace face, recorded as a scroll from top to bottom over 16.5 s. Each section has a centred caption, a bold dark section name followed by a grey "· description". Section 1 (0-3.9 s, frame-locked): caption "Lens · drag it anywhere on the page" at y≈51; below it a 299x178 rounded (≈24 px) card holding a macro photo of an orange-red flower against a pale blue sky with a dark stem, a translucent dark-red chip "Drag the glass anywhere" at its top left, and a ≈124 px circular glass lens that the cursor drags across and off the card: the lens magnifies and bends whatever sits under it (flower inside, the cream page when it hangs past the card edge), has a thin bright rim, a soft drop shadow and no stroke. Below sits a "Depth" slider: grey track with orange fill and a small glass pill thumb. Around 2.5-3.9 s the thumb is dragged right (≈355→432). From 3.9 s the page scrolls in steps: "Frosted glass · toggle frost on every glass" (a 423x303 card playing a swirling gold/white/charcoal silk video, with glass overlays: a "10:56" clock pill, a 4-icon toolbar pill — back arrow, folder, trash, heart — and a round pause button, plus a "Frosted" toggle that flips from grey-off to orange-on at ≈8.0-8.25 s, tinting the glass); "Segmented control · the pill bounces into place" (white pill bar Photos / Music / Files / Mail with a raised glass selection pill that jumps Mail → Files → Music with a bounce, ≈9.2-9.8 s); "Color picker · drag the lens around the wheel" (a conic hue wheel with a small glass lens dragged around it, a swatch tile and a hex label that update, e.g. #3EBBFF → #A3FF7A); "Outset · how far the glass reaches past the letter" (four glass tiles of growing padding around a black "i", labelled 6, 12, { x: 20, y: 14 }, { x: 28, y: 14, top: 32 }); and finally "Notification" (a flower-photo card with a glass banner "Build passed / Deployed to production"). A system cursor is visible throughout.

1v71w2-connectivity-cloud-network-map.summary: A square 1080x1080 light canvas (#fbfbfb) filled edge to edge with a loose, uneven lattice of thin pale-grey outline circles (about 2 px, ~#ececec, no fill, diameters roughly 170 to 240 px). Most circles are empty. Some hold one centred brand icon about 60 to 80 px wide: a dark rounded-square 'lines' app icon, a black cube, a black hexagon cluster, the GitLab fox, a black 'W' wordmark, and further along an orange asterisk, a grey/black door rectangle, a navy outline ghost, a blue-violet terminal cloud, a black ⌘ key tile, the VS Code logo, a purple Terraform mark, a green check, a black Copilot face, a GitHub mark, a red 'M' and a purple bolt. Near the centre sits the hub: a larger solid white disc, about 262 px across, centred near (535,347). It has a soft diffuse drop shadow below and a faint grey rim, and holds the orange/amber Cloudflare cloud. Two to five very faint thin grey straight lines (spokes) radiate from just outside the hub's rim toward nearby icon circles and stop short of them. The motion never stops from about 0.2 s to the end. The whole field of circles streams downward past the hub at roughly 400 to 480 px/s with a slight sideways drift. Each circle moves at a slightly different speed, so the lattice loosens and re-packs. New icon circles enter from the top edge and leave at the bottom, and spokes re-attach to whichever icons are currently nearest. The hub stays put, wandering by no more than about 20 px.

4mdvao-amethyst-glass-card-interaction.summary: A black full-bleed stage with a vertical carousel of six glass credit cards, centred at x 588–1341 (753 px wide, ~473 px tall, ~16 px radius). At rest the active card sits with its top at y≈452 and only its upper ~250 px reads as a card: its lower half is swallowed by a huge theme-coloured light that rises into it as a concave crest (a dark-saturated colour band, then a white-hot core around y 820–950) and flares out below the card's sides as a soft trapezoid cone reaching the frame bottom from x≈200 to x≈1720. The previous card peeks above (top ≈ -100, bottom ≈ 373), dimmed to ~40 % and tinted by the active theme, showing its chip, name in letter-spaced caps and '•••• NNNN'. Cards are dark tinted glass with a thin bright tinted rim, a faint diagonal specular streak, and line-art chip and emblem icons. Chrome: top-left bold white card name plus grey 'NN / 06' counter, top-centre grey hint 'Scroll, drag or use ↑ ↓', top-right rounded dark panel with Background Dark/Light and Material Glass/Metal segmented pills (Dark and Glass selected), and a right-edge column of 6 short ticks with the active one longer and white. Every ~1.43 s (0.65, 1.95, 3.3, 4.75, 6.15, 7.6, 9.05, 10.45 s) the stack slides up one pitch (~552 px) in ~0.5 s with ease-out: the light sinks below the outgoing card (revealing its full face for an instant), the next card rises out of the light, the light recolours to the new theme and climbs back into it; the counter flips first and the name label cross-fades through a blur. Order loops Midnight 01 (blue, horizon-sun) → Amethyst 02 (violet, pyramid) → Verdant 03 (green, leaf) → Ember 04 (orange, four-point star) → Glacier 05 (cyan, three waves) → Graphite 06 (white/grey, ringed planet) → Midnight. During holds the scene drifts up only a few px.

1jed4h-torq-car-diagnostics-landing.summary: A browser-style landing page for the Torq OBD-II dongle sits as a rounded rectangle window (92,164 to 1348,916, ~10px corner radius) floating on a full-bleed backdrop of a dark plum wallpaper (#1e0918) swept by red and orange silk folds across the top and bottom. A fixed top bar runs across the window: the swirl logo with "Torq" on the left at x106, a centred section pill bracketed by corner ticks ("01 | Introduction", later "02 | Capabilities", with a hamburger icon), and on the right a GB flag, a bag icon and a red "Buy Now" button. Scene 1 (0 to 14.6s) is a warm off-white hero (#e7e4da). From 0 to 1s a loader shows: a red hexagon logo over faint hex outlines and a "LOADING RESOURCES" label above a red progress line. It fades to reveal the hero, and the headline letters blur into focus. The hero holds a centred, two-line, near-black headline, "Read Your Car / Like a Device". Below it are a red "Check Compability" button, a grey "Shop Now" button and a "14 days money-back guarantee" line. A photo of a dark-skinned hand holding the frosted TORQ cube sits centred and sways gently on a loop. Thin crosshair guide lines carry "OBD-II SINCE 2026". A large left-aligned dark paragraph sits bottom-left, and two dark product cards ("TORQ Pro" and "TORQ Flet") sit bottom-right. Around 10 to 12.5s the section pill opens a dark maroon dropdown (01 Introduction, 02 Capabilities, 03 Coverage, 04 Vehicles…). Around 14s a dark "TORQ One" hover card pops up beside the hand. From 14.65 to 16s the page scrolls up and a near-black section rises from the bottom edge. Scene 2 (16 to 20.65s) shows huge white type, "TORQ / Bluetooth / 5.2 LE, GATT", overlapping a large 3/4 render of the grey-metallic dongle with an amber glowing side slot. Below the type sit three colour swatches and a 5-row spec table. Thin outlined ISO callouts sit on the right; the hovered one turns red. Five pager dashes sit at the bottom centre. At about 20.7s the dongle turns edge-on and the left column fades. Scene 3 (20.8 to 27.9s), "Factory Options, One Switch Away", puts right-aligned text on the left, the vertical dongle with its glowing amber bar in the centre, and a dark VW/BMW/Toyota/Mercedes card reading "214" on the right. The dongle render slides down to reveal its connector at about 24.5s. From 27.95 to 29.95s the camera pushes into a close-up of the textured metal shell, and the window skews slightly in perspective. Scene 4 shows "What the Dealer Charges an Hour For" on the right, "–$471" with a red bar comparing $69.00 to $540.00 on the left, and pager dash 3 lit red.

ukux5a-motion-corner-menu.summary: A screen recording of a near-empty light page, framed by a slowly moving camera. A white page card (soft vertical gradient #f7f7f7 to #e9e9e9, about 12px corner radius, soft drop shadow) floats over a blurred photo of a beige-grey room with vertical slats on the left and a diagonal shaft of light on the right. In the card's top-right corner sits a small black circular menu button (about 40px at 0.8s) with two short white horizontal lines. From 0 to 0.45s the camera zooms in slightly; from about 1.05 to 1.85s it pushes in toward the top-right corner, so the card's left edge leaves the frame and the button grows to about 54px. The cursor clicks the button at about 2.25s. A black panel then grows out of the button's corner toward the lower left (2.3 to 2.6s). It has rounded corners (about 16px) while it grows and square corners at rest. The panel's contents fade in row by row from the top. At rest (3.2s) the panel is [200,151,628,479]. Its top row has a thin white X close mark at the top right, a small spaced mono "NAVIGATION" at the left and "NULLFORM™" at the right, with a hairline divider under them. The left column holds five numbered rows (01 to 05) in heavy, wide, uppercase white type: START, WORK, STUDIO, JOURNAL, CONTACT. Each row has a small grey ↗ arrow at the right and a hairline divider below it. A vertical hairline separates the right column, which holds a grey mono "CONTACT" label, an email, a phone number, a two-line Berlin address, four grey social icons (Instagram, LinkedIn, X, TikTok) and a white rectangular "START A PROJECT →" button at the bottom. On hover, a row's number and word slide about 12px to the right and its arrow turns white. A hovered social icon brightens from grey to white. The camera pans up about 66px at 3.9 to 4.4s and drifts again at 8.8 to 9.3s. At about 10.3s the X is clicked. The panel shrinks back into the top-right corner, clipping its contents (10.3 to 10.95s), the round button returns, and the camera pulls back out (11.2 to 11.5s).

1uqlj1-local-voice-dictation-pills.summary: A full-bleed, static twilight painting (lavender-violet sky, rows of dark cypress trees down both sides, a terracotta arch in the centre with a pink-orange glow under it) sits behind 8 rows of dark dictation pills. There are 3 pills per row, each row is centred on x≈720, and the row pitch is about 111 px (row centres at y≈150, 262, 373, 485, 597, 708, 820, 931). Each pill is about 90 px tall and fully rounded, with a near-black #121212 body and a soft, semi-translucent dark rim about 5 px wide. Pills are 24 px apart. Each pill is always in one of four states. Recording: a red #f0384a dot plus a 7-bar white waveform with rounded bars that pulse; about 248 px wide. Confirm: a grey circular ✕ button on the left, a waveform, and a white circular ✓ button with a black tick on the right; about 300 px wide. Processing: a grey dot, and the waveform bars collapse into small dots that ripple across. Transcribed: a grey dot, one line of white sans text (about 30 px, medium weight) and a dark-grey round copy button. Over the 12 s loop, pills step through recording → confirm (the ✓ fades in from grey to white) → processing → text, one or two at a time. When a pill changes state its width eases to the new size over about 0.3 s, and the rest of its row slides sideways so the row stays centred. Waveform bars animate all the time. The painting never moves.

1l9xq0-ascii-shark-ai-chat.summary: A light, near-white chat landing page (#f9f9f9) covered edge to edge by a faint square background grid (about 11 x 14.7 px cells, lines a shade darker than the page). The UI is centred on x≈587 and never moves. At the top is a small frosted "History" pill [522,15,131,46] with a clock icon, the word and a chevron, rounded about 10 px with a soft drop shadow. Mid-frame is a thin, light-weight sans heading, "what's on your mind?" (x 322–852, baseline ≈490, about 60 px tall, near-black). Under it is a wide frosted-glass prompt bar [205,524,765,110], radius ≈16, 1 px pale border, translucent pale grey. It holds the placeholder "Ask haj anything..." at the top left, a "+" and a mic icon at the bottom left, and a monospace hint "↵ send · ⇧↵ newline" plus a grey rounded-square send button with a ↗ arrow at the bottom right. A large soft grey elliptical haze (≈900 x 620, centred near the heading and bar) sits behind the UI. The motion is a school of 3–4 sharks (hammerheads and a spotted leopard-type shark) drawn as ASCII art. Each body is a mosaic of axis-aligned grid tiles holding glyphs (S % X t 8 @ # : o). Tile shades run from black through greys to pale, with occasional purple, green, orange or pink tints: some sharks are warm brown-olive, others slate blue-grey. The sharks swim continuously across the whole 24.5 s, bending their bodies, entering and leaving at the frame edges, and snapping cell by cell to the grid. Where a shark passes behind the prompt bar it turns into a soft blurred grey blob, and where it passes under the central haze it fades paler. Sparse dash/dot glyph particles are scattered at the edges and flicker. From ≈9.5 s to ≈14 s the centre is empty, with sharks only at the top-right and bottom-left. From ≈15 s large slate sharks cross the centre again.

16ein-squeezing-progress-bar-animation.summary: A full-bleed flat colour field (saturated blue #2d48f7 while loading) holds three centred-column parts: a big percentage counter at top (x≈620–822, y≈290–365) whose digits are solid and whose '%' sign is the same ink at roughly half opacity; a 14 px-thick progress bar with a round cap running from the left edge of the frame at y≈534–548; and a 108 px outlined circular pause button (two rounded vertical bars inside) centred at x≈721, y≈767. The bar's filled span is echoed by a slightly lighter full-height panel (#3853f5 on blue) whose right edge sits just behind the bar's tip, so the screen reads as split into 'done' and 'to do'. While playing, the counter ticks up about 1% every 30–40 ms and the bar and panel grow rightward in step (tip x ≈ 1442·p + 18). A click on the button (≈0.95 s, again ≈3.5 s) pauses it: over ~0.2 s the whole palette crossfades from blue/white to orange (#f39e2e field, darker #e4932a panel) with near-black brown ink (#211702), the bar's front section springs into an elastic 'squeeze' — the line buckles into a tall narrow S-loop (up ≈65 px, down ≈60 px) plus a small hump just behind the tip, as if the line were compressed against an invisible wall — and the pause glyph morphs into a two-arrow circular refresh icon. Counter and bar freeze (31%, later 81%). A second click (≈1.9 s, ≈4.8 s) crossfades back to blue/white over ~0.2 s while the squeeze relaxes into a decaying soft wave that flattens within ~0.5 s, the refresh icon returns to the pause button, and counting resumes, reaching 98% by 5.43 s. Mid-crossfade frames show a desaturated lavender/brown blend and a ghosted overlap of both icons. All type is a clean geometric sans (medium weight), all strokes have round caps, and nothing has shadow, gradient or outline beyond flat fills; an OS cursor (arrow, then pointing hand over the button) is visible.

sl1t4t-brain-effort-slider.summary: One dark card (≈611×360, radius ≈20, 2px #2a2a2a border, soft black drop shadow) sits centred on a #111 page. Inside, top row: grey "Effort" with a white value word to its right ("Low"→"Medium"→"High"→"Extra"→"Max"→"Galaxy"), and a 34px outlined "?" circle at top right. Below that, grey "Faster" (left) and "Smarter" (right), then a 546×55 rounded #262626 track with six stops at x≈416, 513, 610, 707, 804, 901: grey 6px dots, except stop 2, which is a short vertical light-grey pill marking the recommended setting. Under the track is grey "Recommended". The knob is a ≈62px pink (#f387bb) brain icon with a thick dark-maroon outline. It starts at stop 1 and snaps one stop to the right roughly every 0.55s (≈0.3, 0.85, 1.4, 1.95s), each move ≈150ms. Behind it, a fill that grows from the track's left end runs from dark mauve to pink-purple, then violet as it lengthens. At each step the value word rolls: the old word drifts up, blurs and fades while the new one rises from below and sharpens over ≈250ms. At ≈2.4–2.65s the knob reaches the last stop and the card turns "Galaxy". There is a white flash bloom at the knob. The brain grows to ≈80px and turns into a violet-to-pink gradient with a deep indigo outline and tiny white sparkle squares. The fill becomes a mosaic of ≈8px squares (5 rows): dim navy on the left, brightening to cyan, magenta, lavender and white near the knob. About a dozen dotted rays of tiny squares fan out from the knob, past the card's right edge, over a soft violet glow. The value word turns light blue. From 2.7s to the end, the squares and rays twinkle in place. Nothing else moves.

11wbjw-save-button-that-ages.summary: A single blue pill-shaped "Save" button is centred on an off-white (#fdfdfd) page. It sits at about x 445–977, y 426–655 (533 x 229 px), with fully round ends and a thin dark navy outline. The fill is a glossy saturated blue (#315ee8): slightly lighter along the top edge, slightly darker along the bottom, with a faint soft radial sheen on the right half. The centred label "Save" is a bold sans in near-white (#e9f6ff), about 60 px cap height, spanning x 622–800. The story is wear from use. The button is clean from 0 to about 1.1 s. A macOS pointing-hand cursor then clicks it repeatedly at the right of the label from about 1.15 to 3.8 s. On each press the whole pill scales down about 2% (to about x 455–967) and springs back. Thin pale hairline scratches build up across the face with the clicks. Around 4.1 s two dark specks appear right of "e", and by 4.6 s they become a jagged worn-through patch (about 808–890 x 515–592). The patch shows grainy tan/ochre material under the blue, with a dark scorched rim. The cursor leaves as an arrow at the top-left (about 5.3 s), then returns as a hand. It clicks the top-left shoulder from about 6.0 to 8.3 s, and a second, bigger tan chip peels away the top-left of the pill (about 460–580 x 428–492). It then goes back to clicking the right patch until the end. Nothing else moves: the button stays centred and the page stays blank.

135634-dreamy-anime-ai-desktop-app.summary: A static macOS-style desktop window (x 178–1545, y 76–1006, ~14px corner radius, no visible border) floats over a full-bleed painted anime landscape: lush green hillside trees on the left, overhead power wires crossing the top, a wooden utility pole at the right and a grassy meadow with yellow flowers along the bottom. Inside the window the top ~60% is a painted pastel sky (cobalt-blue with pink/peach cumulus clouds, denser cloud banks at both sides framing a clear blue centre) overlaid with a fine halftone dot grid (~5px pitch) that is most visible in the clouds and blue; the sky dissolves through a soft white mist into a pale sage-cream base (#d2ddc7–#dae1db) filling the lower half. Top-left sits a frosted lavender pill holding the red/yellow/green traffic lights, a sidebar icon and back/forward arrows. Centred at y≈470–587 is a 731×117 frosted, light grey-white prompt bar with ~16px radius: placeholder "Do anything...", a paperclip at bottom-left, and at bottom-right an orange asterisk mark, "Opus 5.5" in dark semibold, "High" in grey and a 28px black circular send button with a white up arrow. Small grey context chips sit above it at right ("personal-metal", "comet") and below it at left ("Current checkout", "main"), all ~12px Inter-like type with chevrons. Nothing in the window moves for the whole 4.77s. The only motion is in the background painting: a yellow-and-green vintage tram (car number "305") slides right-to-left behind the window from ~0.3s, its nose appearing at the right edge, passing behind the window (never visible through it) and emerging at the left by ~1.2s, its last car clearing the left edge by ~2.3s; the overhead wires and foliage sway faintly throughout.

1ce71v-minimalist-portfolio-reveal.summary: A light, near-white page (#fbfcfa) split into two zones. On the left, a static block of introductory copy starts at x=82, y≈400. It is seven lines of a geometric grotesk (Space Grotesk–like, ~28px, ~41.5px line pitch, max width ≈1005px). Lines alternate between near-black (#0f100d) primary phrases and mid-grey (#a0a09f) secondary clauses. Three inline brand marks sit in the text: a small knot icon before "soft machine", "interior[.]dev" with blue square brackets around a dot, and a black bar glyph followed by the serif wordmark "behindyou". The last line has four rounded pastel highlight pills: yellow "inspiration", blue "writing", green "x" and lavender "github". On the right (x≈1190–1570), a single column of rounded project cards (~320×205px, radius ~16px, very soft shadow) is set with alternating small horizontal offsets and a slight tilt or perspective of about 1–2°. The cards are, top to bottom: a blue settings-menu card, a light-grey card with a lego-brick notification, a black card with a toast and progress dots, a light card with a curved carousel of B/W photos, a white card with a curved carousel of album covers, and later a "loading workspace" card. Each card plays its own screen recording of a micro-interaction. The only layout motion is the card column. It scrolls upward continuously and linearly at ≈44–45 px/s for the whole 8.77s clip, about 385px in total, with no pauses and no easing. Cards leave off the top edge and new ones enter from the bottom. The text block never moves.

1c6gvh-refero-pro-upgrade-success-modal.summary: A success modal over a dimmed Refero web page. The backdrop is the page under a flat grey-violet scrim (#6b6e82): a sidebar at top left ("iOS apps", "Styles" with a "Beta" pill), a large serif hero headline that peeks out right of the modal ("…r the AI Era", later "…ning next?"), a search card with an × and a round arrow button, and two columns of suggestion links with hooked-arrow icons at the bottom. Centred at x 475–1176, y 87–962 is a white modal card with about 24px radius. Its top third (y ≈110–410) holds a huge "PRO" wordmark drawn as a heat-map gradient: dark navy cores fade out through cyan, yellow/orange and red to a magenta fringe and then white. The edges are soft, blurred and grainy, there is no outline, and the O is clipped by the card's right edge. Below sit a two-line centred serif headline, "You're Pro." / "No more walls." (about 70px, near-black), two lines of grey sans body copy and a full-width black "Keep researching" button (radius ≈12). Motion: only the PRO wordmark animates, on a loop of about 4.3s. A blob grows from the left edge and writes P, then R, then O from left to right (0–2s). PRO holds complete (~2–2.8s). A wipe then dissolves it from the left: P melts to magenta and orange, then R goes (~2.9–4s), while O stays. P reappears and the cycle repeats (full again at ~6.2s, ~10.5s, ~14.7s). 14yr7r-minimal-crypto-asset-swap.summary: A light product-demo shell on a #fafafa page: on the left a large rounded stage [50,52,1056,982] in pale grey #eaeaec with a small segmented pill (cube / code icons) top-left, bookmark and speaker icons top-right and a white round play button bottom-right; on the right a white settings panel [1126,52,459,982] titled "Asset swap" with a two-line grey description, three segmented toggles (Fill Light/Dark, Stroke Off/On, Assets Crypto/Currency), two filled-bar sliders (Bounce 30, Corner 28px), an outlined "Share" button and a black "Add to bench 1" button. Centred in the stage is the swap widget: two stacked white cards 614 px wide and 222 px tall with ~40 px corners and a 6 px seam, "You pay 0.05 / $4,885.00 / BTC" over "You receive 127.496 / $4,870.35 / HYPE", amounts at ~44 px dark, labels and fiat in grey, each coin in a light grey pill with a round coloured logo; a 76 px light-grey circle carrying a black arrow straddles the seam, and a soft blurred blue/pink/green glow sits behind the cards' right edge. Type is a neutral grotesk (Inter-like), dark #151517 on white. Motion is all inside the stage, the right panel never changes: at 2.5–2.75 s tapping the BTC pill makes the pay card grow downward into a 450 px tall coin picker (header "You pay", close X, five rows BTC Bitcoin, ETH Ethereum, HYPE Hyperliquid, ZEC Zcash, QNT Quant, with a check on the current coin) while the receive card squashes and fades beneath it; the list fades in. Hovered rows get a pale grey rounded highlight. At ~4.4–4.65 s picking HYPE collapses the picker back into two cards with a springy overshoot (top card briefly reaches y≈598) and the values become 100 HYPE $3,820.00 / 0.03898 BTC $3,808.54. Tapping the arrow flips it (down↔up) and swaps the cards' contents in place (by 6.6 s "You receive 127.496 HYPE" sits over "You pay 0.05 BTC"; by 7.6 s it is back to "You pay 100 HYPE / You receive 0.03898 BTC"); the cards themselves don't move. At 8.5–8.75 s the receive card grows upward into a "You receive" picker (its top passes y≈362 at 8.63 s and reaches 318 at 9.3 s), and at 9.8–10 s choosing QNT closes it to 36.445 QNT. The demo then repeats this with ZEC (40 ZEC / 19.997 QNT, flipped to 39.766 ZEC / 20 QNT).

1ymuts-sports-photo-gallery-interaction.summary: An off-white (#f3f3f1) page holds a centred 4-column × 3-row grid of 12 portrait sports photos. Each tile is 192×241 px with about an 8 px corner radius. Columns start at x=306/518/730/941 and rows at y=155/415/675, with gaps of about 20 px, so the grid spans 306–1133 × 155–916. The photos are a mix of monochrome and colour: Seahawks player in a dome, a Jordan dunk in black and white, two golfers in white caps, a tennis player on a blue court, a pitcher in black and white, a golfer in red celebrating in front of a scoreboard, a batter on a dark teal field with a red ground band, a crouching golfer in black and white, a motion-blurred 49ers QB, a purple-toned football throw, an outfielder on green grass and a tennis forehand in black and white. A soft near-white cursor dot about 28 px wide, with a blurred grey rim, glides around the page. Each click opens the clicked tile (about 0.25 s, ease-out). It grows into a 555×694 px card centred on the grid at (720,535) with a soft drop shadow beneath it. At the same moment the whole page behind it dims to flat grey #696b68: the other 11 tiles darken with the page and drift a few px outward with slight perspective skew, and they stay partly visible around the card. A second click (about 1 s later, cursor still in place) reverses this in about 0.2 s and the page returns to #f3f3f1. bwl3yk-paper-fold-portfolio-page.summary: A single portfolio page drawn as a sheet of off-white paper (#fcfcfc) with postage-stamp scalloped edges, sitting on a slightly darker grey ground with a soft drop shadow; the sheet runs from about x 25 to 1595 and from y 25 off the bottom of the frame. At rest (5.4s, 7.75s) the left column holds a small scalloped hand-drawn stamp (red house, blue and green scribbles, "4:00", "NYC", "Jm.sv", ":)") at about 135,155. A text column starts at x 524: the handwritten all-caps name "JAMES CLEMENTS", a three-line sans-serif bio with underlined links "Vercel" and "Old Friends", a grey handwritten "WRITING" label, then a list row with the handwritten title "SKILLS ARE SOFTWARE" (thin grey underline) and a grey "OCT 5" date at the right, x 1156. The motion is all one gesture: the top sheet is peeled back like paper, dragged by the cursor. The flap's back is plain white, and its scalloped edge is printed with three offset coloured scallop rows (blue, green, red). A soft grey shadow follows the crease. Under the sheet is a second page laid out as a 3×2 grid: a large copy of the stamp (about 320 px) at the top left, and five pale grey scalloped placeholder tiles, each with a grey "?". Order of events: 0 to 3.1s, a diagonal corner peel from the top-right sweeps in and out; around 1s the fold turns horizontal and covers the top band down to about y 490. The flap falls back flat by about 4.85s, and the page rests flat 4.9 to 5.85s. From 5.9 to 7.1s a horizontal top-edge fold drops to about y 380 and lifts again; the page rests again 7.15 to 8.35s. From 8.4 to 9.05s a big top-right peel sweeps over almost the whole sheet and shows the grid page under it, with a curl left at the bottom-left around 9.7s. From 10.15 to 10.65s the sheet flops back over the grid through a horizontal fold, and the page ends flat.

x0r410-shader-driven-workflow-hero.summary: A cropped Cloudflare-style product hero on a 1080 square. A 92 px nav bar runs across the top: a cropped "s ⌄" at the left edge, then "Resources ⌄", "Enterprise", "Pricing", a red "Under attack?" with an alert-circle icon, "Log in", and an orange pill button reading "Start building" (764,30,123,34). Below the nav, the left edge shows a cropped headline ("ulti-" / "s.", about 48 px) and two cropped body paragraphs. The middle and right hold the hero canvas, x≈152–934 and y≈92–828, on a faint 92 px grid. In the canvas a procedural shader draws a field of vertical bar particles, 8 px apart. Each bar is a thick red-orange core segment with thin amber or yellow tails, and the bars build 3-D-looking blobs and slabs. A diagonal dotted "wire" of short bars links the blobs from bottom-left to top-right, so the whole thing reads as a workflow graph. Thin 1 px orange rectangles frame two of the blobs, each with an orange tag in white mono type giving a coordinate pair (e.g. "210, 287"), and a thin orange line connects the two boxes. A narrow right rail (x 934–1080) carries a grey mono "HERO" label and tiny red tick dots. A bordered logo row at y≈910–1047 holds Uber, DoorDash, Shopify, Discord, OpenAI, Lovable and Anthropic, and it scrolls left continuously at about 45 px/s for the whole clip. The shader blobs and their boxes morph and travel without stopping. The page theme flips three times, each time with a horizontal stripe band (orange, red, purple, blue, green, thin amber) that sweeps from the bottom to the top in about 0.23 s and eases out. Behind the band the page turns from light #fdfdfd to dark #121212 at 3.75–3.98 s, back to light at about 6.95–7.15 s, and dark again at about 9.4–9.6 s, where it stays to the end. In light mode the particle cores are red and the halo is pale yellow. In dark mode they glow amber-orange over dark red.

6amwj2-portfolio-animations.summary: A single-column light portfolio page (#f9f9f9 background, content column about x 352–936 at normal scale) recorded as a screen capture with editor camera zooms. A floating white pill (about 292x48, fully rounded, soft drop shadow) sits fixed at top centre: round avatar, "Colin Lienard" with a grey subtitle that swaps as you scroll ("Full-Stack Engineer" → "France and remote" → email → "9:22 PM (Paris)") and a "⌘K" hint at the right. Under it: an italic serif name "Colin Lienard", three paragraphs of grey sans text with dark highlighted phrases ("full-stack engineer", "Limoges, France", "remotely", "startups and scaleups", "front-end", "back-end", "open-source"), a dark "Copy my email" button and four grey social icons, a faint wavy divider, then sections Experience (timeline entries, bullet lists with dashed-underlined hover terms, tech chips), Open-Source (2x2 soft cards with 3D mascot renders and star counts), Tech Stack (icon grid) and a copyright footer. Motion: at 0.5s the pill's text blur-fades in; from about 1.4s to 6.9s the camera zooms ~1.5x on the intro while the cursor hovers social links and floating white hover cards pop up (GitHub profile card with banner and Follow, a freelance card "Available for freelance work / €450/day / France and remote / React TypeScript Node", a LinkedIn card with blue banner and Connect, a GitHub contributions heatmap); from about 7s the page scrolls down through Experience (a dark tooltip appears over "Led several key technical migrations."), Open-Source and Tech Stack, with content blurring as it leaves under the pill and blur-fading in at the bottom. Around 16.5s ⌘K morphs the pill into a command menu (Sections Home/Experience/Open-Source/Tech Stack, Language Français ↗, Theme Light/Dark/System); a black rounded keystroke overlay at bottom centre shows the keys pressed. At about 20.5s the theme switches to dark (whole page and menu go near-black), at about 21.85s back to light, and at about 23.4s Enter on Home collapses the menu back into the pill while the page scrolls back toward the top.

ev3140-interactive-isometric-data-cards.summary: Three portrait stat cards sit in a single centred row on a flat charcoal page (#28282a): each is about 450x561 px with chamfered (diagonally cut, ~10 px) corners rather than rounded ones. The left edges are at x≈266, 734 and 1202, the gap is 18 px, and the top/bottom edges are at y≈261/822. Each card has a bold grotesk title at top left ("Productive days", "Spending patterns", "Busiest hours", ~30 px) and a tiny grey monospace index at top right ("001", "002", "003"). Below that, four L-shaped corner brackets frame a square chart area with a faint dot-star field. Inside the frame is an isometric thin-line wireframe illustration: 7 stepped bar boxes with an orange marker dot, an exploded pie with one orange slab slice, and a lighthouse on a tick-marked dial casting an orange light cone. Resting cards are near-black (#1b1b1e) with cream line-work and light type. The card under the cursor turns cream (#e7dfd1) with dark type and dark line-work, and tilts slightly in 3D toward the pointer. Its chart reacts too: the orange dot hops to the hovered bar, the hovered pie slice lifts and turns orange, and the lighthouse beam swings to point at the cursor. When hover passes to another card, the old card and the new card both cross-fade through a flat warm grey (~#77716d) over ~0.3 s. A card that has lost hover keeps its last orange highlight (bar 7 lit with its dot, the pie quarter laid flat in orange). Hover order: card 1 (0–2.5 s), card 2 (2.9–6.0 s), card 3 (6.35–11.7 s, with a grey flicker at 9.55–10.1 s as the cursor grazes its bottom edge), then back to card 1 (~12.35–13.85 s), and all cards are dark at the end.

Under the tabs is a wide, slightly lighter panel (#222227, x 169–1222, y 277–796, small radius). It holds a staggered grid of dim, dark ID cards (radius ≈12) in five columns: partly clipped strips at both edges, two full columns at x 272–532 and 860–1118 (rows y≈347–519 and 554–726), and a centre column at x 566–826 with a card pitch of 207 px. Each dim card carries a faint swap logo top-left, faint NFC arcs top-right, and a line of monospaced scrambled characters bottom-left that re-randomises every few frames. The centre card (y 451–623) is the hero. It is a lighter grey frosted-glass ID card with a top-lit gradient and a thin white outer ring offset about 3 px outside its own edge. It shows a crisp white swap logo, white NFC arcs, a pale line drawing of a classical building (3 window rows by 4 bays, arched ground floor) with ghosted angled panels at both sides, a small grey department label and a white name. Below the panel is a four-column feature row (x 169, 439, 709, 980; icons at y≈842, text from y≈876). Each column has a bold white lead-in followed by grey body copy. Column 1 has a small static spinner glyph at its top right (x≈391). Motion is a loop of about 2.9 s per card. The page, headline, tabs, side columns and feature row never move. 14ybn1-cinematic-calendar-booking-page.summary: A full-bleed time-lapse video of the Golden Gate Bridge with the San Francisco skyline fills the 1908x1080 frame. In the top left is a small dark pill reading "‹ Home" at (47,20). Below it sits a frosted-glass booking card. The card's left edge is at x=47 and its top at y=99, with a radius of about 32px. The glass is a smoky dark tint that blurs whatever is behind it. At rest the card is 443x581 and holds "30 min · Google Meet", a bold white "Book a time", a grey subtitle, a September 2026 month grid with 30 days, and a translucent "Pick a day" pill. On the right side of the frame, right-aligned to x≈1852, a lock-screen-style widget shows a date line, a huge thin-bold white clock ("11:21", about 135px tall), and a green dot followed by "San Francisco". At about 1.8s the cursor clicks 30. That day turns into a white disc, and over about 0.15s the card widens to 863px and grows down to 887px tall. It gains a right column with "WEDNESDAY / September 30 / 26 times available", a close ×, and an hourly timeline from 8 AM to 12 AM. The timeline has hatched unavailable bars at 10 AM, 1 PM, 2–3 PM ("Busy") and 7 PM. The left button becomes "Pick a time" at y=900, and the date line changes to "Wednesday, September 30". From about 2.95s the cursor sweeps up and down the timeline. A thin horizontal hover line follows it, with a black pill at its right end giving the exact time (for example "9:25 PM") and a ghost slot label. The clock digits follow the hovered time, and the background video crossfades to that time of day: midday blue, sunset orange, purple dusk, night with lit bridge traffic. At about 11.5s the 6:30 slot is clicked. It becomes a white pill reading "6:30 – 7:00 PM", and the bottom of the left column shows a summary box ("Wed, Sep 30 / 6:30 – 7:00 PM / Pacific Time") above a white "Continue" pill. At about 14.0s the left column is replaced by a "Your details" form: "‹ Back", a Date/Time summary box, Name, Email and topic fields, and a white "Confirm" pill. The timeline stays, and hovering keeps changing the sky and the clock until the end.

109pwi-blur-fade-animations.summary: A browser-window-sized page (1296x810 at x72-1368, y135-945, square corners) floats centred over a full-bleed, coarsely dithered/pixelated painting of a golden Gothic spire, clouds and crags. The page is a law-firm site in two sections. The first is a flat oxblood #53120f hero with a soft warm radial glow behind a centred block: a small cream round icon with the eyebrow "Growth Brings Complexity. We Bring Clarity." in small serif, a 4-line cream serif headline "Our advisory model is built to / catch risk before it becomes a / liability, so your business can scale / with confidence.", then a rotating feature (serif title plus a 2-line sans description), a cream icon disc with two small cream satellite dots sitting at the apex of a large faint dashed semicircular arc, and a muted monochrome logo row (Google, cuts off and fades at the left, coinbase, Uber, Medium). When zoomed out, thin vertical ruler rails with tiny rotated numbers show inside the left and right edges. The second section is cream #eeede1: a "What We Do" eyebrow with a maroon gavel badge, the maroon serif heading "Full-spectrum corporate counsel", a sans sub-line, a 4-item serif accordion list divided by hairlines, a maroon "Take Consultation >" button with a drop shadow and a serif line "Consult with us about your needs". A sepia photo of a blindfolded Lady Justice statue holding scales fills the right half and fades into the cream at the bottom. Motion is all blur-fade: 0 to 1.1s the hero scrolls up into place (top edge from about y396 to y135) while the headline lines un-blur one after another, top to bottom. About 1.6 to 1.85s the whole page scales up about 1.2x from centre, so the rails leave the frame and the headline grows from about 470 to about 565 px wide. The feature text swaps by blurring out and in line by line while the icon disc slides counter-clockwise along the dashed arc: the old disc exits down the left side and the new one rises from the bottom right to the apex (about 1.9 to 2.8s: bank to handshake, "Risk Assessment & Prevention" to "Dedicated Advisory Partnership"; about 4.5 to 5.7s: handshake to lightbulb, to "Rapid Response & Resolution"). About 6.1 to 6.35s it scales back down. 7.3 to 8.9s the cream section scrolls up from the bottom over the hero, its content arriving heavily blurred and sharpening. 9.3 to 9.8s it scales up about 1.2x again, the first accordion row "Mergers & Acquisitions" darkens and opens a description under the cursor, and "Consult with us about your needs" un-blurs word by word. 11.1 to 11.45s it scales back down.

16430q-drag-shift-file-converter.summary: A screen-recorded macOS concept on the stock orange-red-yellow-violet Sonoma-style gradient wallpaper. It opens on a silver MacBook Pro mockup with a notch, on white. The camera pushes into the screen (0–1.8s) while a file icon, "Page 001.pdf", is dragged. Holding shift during the drag opens a radial menu centred on the cursor. The menu is a translucent frosted warm-glass disc with a thin golden rim. Inside the rim sit cream-to-peach petal segments with dark bold caps labels, around a hollow centre ring holding a frosted pill that shows the file size and then the hovered target. The first menu has 4 segments (DOCX top, JPG right, PNG bottom, TXT left). The hovered segment fills with a saturated red-orange gradient and its label turns white. Dropping on JPG creates "Page 001.jpg". Dragging that file opens an 8-segment image-format ring (PNG, WEBP, HEIC, TIFF, AVIF, BMP, PDF, DOCX). It then switches to a 7-segment action ring with line icons (COMPRESS, METADATA, EDIT, ANNOTATE, ADD BG, CROP, REDACT; centre "1.2 MB"). Choosing CROP zooms into a "Crop Image" sheet: a warm-gradient rounded window with the document page, a red crop frame with square corner handles, a grey dimmed outside area, an aspect-ratio segmented control (Free active in red), W/H fields, and Reset and Apply. The crop frame is dragged down about 46px between 8.05 and 8.55s. Apply produces "Page 001 Cropped.jpg". It is dragged again through the format ring and the action ring (CROP, then ADD BG highlighted). That opens an "Add BG" sheet with a gradient preview, swatch rows, Padding/Corners/Shadow sliders and Save with Background. Padding is dragged from 160 to 609 px while the camera drifts. The clip ends on the desktop with four files in a row: Page 001.pdf, Page 001.jpg, Page 001 Cropped.jpg, and "Page 001 Cropped With Ba...ound.png". Type is SF Pro throughout. Filename labels are white with a shadow, or white on blue #2a5fd6 selection pills while dragged.

1dff4c-frame-controls-popover-ui.summary: A cropped, warm-cream web page (giant black "ion." headline top-left, grey body copy, an orange-to-coral vertical stripe at x≈1155-1192, a "A comment" card top-right, a yellow "Se…" button, a coral band across y≈668-802) sits behind a light-grey dotted canvas strip at the bottom. A white floating toolbar (x 104-1527, y 893-1047, radius ≈28) holds pointer (selected, grey tile), hand, split, a divider, "Landsc… 3:2", "Desktop 1440", a hatched-corner frame icon, a rainbow-gradient circle, a divider, download and settings icons. Above it one white popover (bottom edge fixed at y≈855, small downward caret pointing at the active toolbar button) morphs between panels: Device (Size/Scale/Scroll rows + Fit preview), Format (Standard/Social segmented control, 8 aspect tiles with Landscape 3:2 selected), a background palette grid, and Frame (Padding 70/70, Corners 47/47, Shadow 7-stop slider, Cut Where 60% / Gap 20) beside a dotted "Preview" pane with a grey mock page inside a rainbow-gradient border crossed by thin dark diagonal hatch lines. Each switch (≈150-250 ms) resizes the popover box, slides the caret to the new button, and crossfades the content with a heavy gaussian blur on the outgoing/incoming panel. Typography is a rounded geometric sans (Nunito-like), dark grey labels, near-black values in a monospace-ish numeral face with slashed zero. Later a cursor hovers to show black pill tooltips ("Where the shadow falls", "One box per side", "One box per corner"), a click shows a blue ring, the preview card re-renders its corners, the whole view zooms in ≈2.2x around 15.5-16.2s and back out ≈20.6-21.3s, padding splits into two rows of per-side inputs, and near 28s the shadow row expands with Angle/Distance/Blur/Opacity fields and a light-aim preview.

17n5mv-assets-overview-carousel.summary: A white (#fdfdfd) square stage holds a centred iPhone mockup (white rim, black bezel, Dynamic Island) running a dark chat app called "Tickr". The top half of the screen is a saturated blue (#085ff5) card with rounded bottom corners (~40px): status bar 9:41, a nav row (back chevron in a translucent circle, centred bold white "Tickr", chart and gear icons in translucent circles), then a large sentence mixing dim pale-blue words with bold white words and inline avatars/emoji ("Hey, prosku.a / Your file is • In Progress – edits by … You have 5 unread comments and scheduled 1 meeting."), a dotted divider, and a meta row "3 hours ago • 12 • 14 • 2" with paperclip, images and link icons. Below on black: a grabber, a blurred segmented pill, a dim grey prompt paragraph, a white reply paragraph with a purple glowing icon, two dark suggestion chips and an "Ask to build..." input. Motion: at ~1.0s a translucent touch dot taps the images "14" count; from ~1.25s square image tiles pour out from under the blue card at the right and run down a curved vertical carousel (a drum: the centre tile ~154px is largest and closest to the screen centre, tiles above and below shrink, step right along an arc and tilt a few degrees, the top ones slide under the blue card). At the same time the black area behind the carousel blurs and dims (the blue card stays sharp), and two round dark buttons (share arrow, download arrow) appear left of the centre tile. From 1.45s to 2.3s the whole phone zooms in about 1.5x and pans up so the meta row sits near the top of the frame. The carousel keeps scrolling downward and settles with the tongue photo centred (hold 2.85-3.85s); some tiles are live (the portrait tile changes face while held). From 3.9s to 4.25s a drag (grey touch dot moving down) scrolls the drum down two slots so the blue chair drawing is centred. From 4.75s to 5.65s the camera zooms back out with motion blur to the original framing, and by ~6.1s the carousel is gone and the screen is back to the opening state, ready to loop.
